purpose: Test whether a stationary LinUCB scheduler benefits from contextual mutation-family structure and how it behaves after an abrupt reward-model shift, without claiming evidence from a real fuzzer or target binary.

rewardModel.distribution: Bernoulli with probabilities from a logistic contextual model

interpretationBoundary: The simulator does not execute AFL++, libFuzzer, or any target binary.
Synthetic Bernoulli rewards are only a proxy for useful mutation outcomes such as coverage novelty or reproducible faults.
The LinUCB implementation is stationary and has no forgetting/change-point mechanism, so abrupt-drift behavior is intentionally stress-tested rather than hidden.
CPU scheduler overhead, executions per second, real coverage, and fault discovery are not measured.
This manifest defines an exploratory pilot rather than a preregistered confirmatory study.
